the achievable performance in terms of correct-detection probability and the associated MAT are both reduced as the number of the transmit antennas is increased, while maintaining a given total transmitted power.

, in contrast with the common belief that the number of antennas is always beneficial for the initial code acquisition, increasing the number of antennas in a DS-CDMA downlink system can actually degrade the achievable performance, which, in turn, can be detrimental to the overall system performance, especially when the system is required to operate at low signal-to-noise ratios.

the MAT is a nondecreasing and nonconcave function of the number transmit antennas, which implies that the optimal number of transmit antennas for a given system configuration is not necessarily the maximum number of transmit antennas.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the multiple-transmit/multiple-receive antennas-aided DS-CDMA system should be designed with a large number of antennas, but the total transmit power should be kept low.
, in our considered system scenario, increasing the number of multiple transmit antennas is beneficial in terms of the system throughput, but detrimental in terms of the initial code acquisition.

, when maintaining a given total power, the use of multiple transmit antennas does not provide any advantage over single-transmit-antenna operation in terms of the achievable code-acquisition performance, but, when maintaining a constant signal power, it provides a performance gain in terms of the required signal energy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the multiple transmit antennas are beneficial in terms of the achievable bit-error-ratio (BER) performance but not in terms of the MAT.

the multiple-transmit/multiple-receive antenna-aided DS-CDMA system should be designed to attain its target performance at the lowest possible signal power, which is possible when the number of transmit and receive antennas is increased.
, when employing multiple transmit antennas, the MAT is not a good metric for characterizing the initial-code-acquisition performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in contrast with the common perception, the performance of the serial-search-based acquisition process degrades as the number of antennas is increased.
, for a given target bit-error ratio, the number of antennas must be carefully chosen to minimize the MAT while simultaneously maximizing the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR).
it is not always beneficial to employ more transmit antennas when communicating with the same target performance.
